colima_config.title: Colima Configuration
colima_config.description: Edit colima.yaml directly. Settings you have added by hand are preserved; changes take effect on the next restart.
colima_config.network_address: Assign a reachable IP address to the VM
colima_config.saved: Config saved. Restart the instance to apply.
colima_config.not_saved: Config not saved — fix the errors above.

issue.cpu_zero: CPU count must be at least 1.
issue.cpu_over_host: Requested {cpu} CPUs but the host has {host}. The VM will contend with the host for cores.
issue.memory_zero: Memory must be at least 1 GiB.
issue.memory_over_host: Requested {memory} GiB of a {host} GiB host. Leave at least 2 GiB for the host.
issue.disk_zero: Disk size must be at least 1 GiB.
issue.disk_shrink: Disk cannot shrink from {from} GiB to {to} GiB. Colima can only grow a disk.
issue.disk_over_free: Requested {disk} GiB but only {free} GiB is free on the host.

ai.empty_title: Hi! I'm your Colima AI Assistant.
ai.empty_hint: I can control containers, troubleshoot issues, read the knowledge bank, and manage your VMs.
ai.input_hint: Enter to send · Shift+Enter for a new line
ai.bubble_working: Colima AI is working — click to open

terminal.ensure_running: Make sure the instance is running.

diagnose.no_file: No compose file recorded for this project.
diagnose.valid: docker compose config reports no problems with this file.
diagnose.anti_pattern: Known bad advice — do not do this
diagnose.no_kb_match: Nothing in the Knowledge Bank matches this error. You can ask your configured AI provider instead.
diagnose.redaction_note: Environment values, secrets and env_file contents are removed before sending. Review the exact text below first — nothing leaves your machine until you press Ask AI.
diagnose.no_ai_config: Configure an AI provider in Settings first.
diagnose.autofix_desc: Apply the fix to your compose file automatically, not just read the diagnosis.

autofix.none: No safe automatic fix for this error. The diagnosis above explains the cause; this one needs a human edit.
autofix.comments_lost: This fix rewrites the file structure and will remove your comments.
autofix.partial: This fixes one problem but the file still fails validation:
autofix.applied: Fix applied. You can undo it.
autofix.refused: A proposed fix was blocked because it would have removed:

gate.default_desc: This is a ColimaUI Pro feature.
gate.free_note: Everything you use today stays free, including commercial use. Pro is optional.

consent.title: Help improve ColimaUI?
consent.body: Share anonymous usage events so we know which features to improve. Never your container names, paths, environment variables, chat contents, or keys.
consent.default_off: It's off unless you turn it on, and you can change this anytime in Settings.

settings.title: Privacy & Telemetry
settings.desc: Anonymous usage events, off by default. Never container names, paths, environment variables, chat contents, or keys.
settings.on: On — nothing is transmitted yet; there is no endpoint.

account.title: Account
account.signed_out_desc: You are not signed in. An account only puts your name on this app — every feature works without one.
account.readonly_note: Your name and picture come from your sign-in provider. Change them there and they update here.
account.ephemeral_note: This session cannot be saved securely on this system, so you will need to sign in again next launch.

signin.title: Sign in to ColimaUI
signin.subtitle: Signing in is optional — it only puts your name on this app. Your first sign-in creates the account.
signin.no_unlock: Signing in is how Pro reaches you. Your subscription follows your account, and keeps working offline.
signin.waiting: Finish signing in in your browser, then come back here.

unavailable.browser: Sign-in is only available in the ColimaUI desktop app — it needs the system browser and your keychain.
unavailable.unconfigured: Accounts are not configured in this build yet.

subscription.title: Subscription
subscription.offline_note: Pro keeps working offline, and stays active if you sign out.
subscription.lapsed: Your subscription is no longer active.
subscription.signin_first: You will be asked to sign in first.
subscription.free_desc: You are on the free plan — the whole app, including commercial use. Pro adds optional AI-powered fixes.
subscription.checkout_unavailable: Checkout is unavailable right now. Nothing was charged.
subscription.checkout_unlinked: This purchase will not be linked to your account and will not unlock Pro.

plans.not_configured: Paid plans are not available yet. Everything in the app today stays free.

pro.name: Pro
pro.blurb: Everything in Free, plus optional AI-powered fixes. One seat.

teams.name: Pro Teams
teams.blurb: The same Pro features for your team, from 2 seats. Manage seats in the billing portal.

updates.title: Updates
updates.browser_only: Automatic updates are available in the desktop app.
updates.desc: Check for a newer signed build. Updates are verified before they are applied.
updates.up_to_date: You are on the latest version.
updates.installed: Update installed. Restart ColimaUI to finish.

topology.title: Topology
topology.empty: No Docker resources found for the current engine.

transfer.overwrite: Replace the file if it already exists
transfer.copy_out_is_archive: Saved as a .tar archive — a folder and a single file both arrive that way. Extract it with: tar -xf <file>

activity.title: Activity
activity.history_feature_desc: Keep samples on disk and look at last night, not just right now.
activity.history_empty: No history recorded for this range yet.
activity.history_not_recording: History is not being recorded on this install.
activity.history_dropped: {count} batches were dropped because the disk could not keep up — the gaps below are real.
activity.alerts_feature_desc: Be told when a container stays over a threshold, instead of finding out later.
activity.no_alert_events: Nothing has fired yet. That is the intended state.
activity.no_rules: No rules yet. The form below creates one.
activity.backtest_result: Would have fired {count} times across {samples} stored samples.
activity.backtest_no_data: No history stored for that window yet, so there is nothing to test against.
activity.backtest_caveat: Anything older than an hour is stored as per-minute averages, so brief spikes count for less here than they will live.
activity.history_paused: Recording paused while the subscription was inactive. What was already stored is untouched.

actions.empty: Nothing recorded yet. Actions that change this machine show up here.
actions.partial: Some history could not be read:
actions.export_desc: Take the log somewhere else — JSON or CSV — and keep a longer window of it.
actions.dest_prompt: Folder to save the history in

diagnostics.title: Report a problem
diagnostics.lead: Nothing is sent automatically. Review everything below, uncheck anything you would rather not share, then copy or save it.
diagnostics.truncated: {bytes} bytes of older log lines were trimmed.
diagnostics.dest_prompt: Folder to save the report in
diagnostics.paste_hint: Paste the report you copied from the app here, or attach the saved file.

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.empty_hint: Transfers and alerts show up here.
notifications.settings_description: Transfers keep running in the background. ColimaUI can tell your operating system when one finishes, so you find out without switching back.
notifications.os_enabled: Notify me when a transfer finishes
notifications.os_hint: Only while the ColimaUI window is in the background, and only that a transfer ended — never its file paths or error output.
notifications.os_desktop_only: System notifications need the desktop app. In the browser, the bell in the sidebar shows the same thing.
notifications.announcements_enabled: Show release notes and security advisories
notifications.announcements_hint: ColimaUI checks a file on GitHub every few hours. Nothing about you is sent — but the request itself shows GitHub your IP address and the time. Switching this off stops the request entirely.

volumes.prune_confirm: Remove all unused volumes? This cannot be undone.

security.title: Security
security.subtitle: Scan a local image and see why it scores what it does
security.scanner_missing_text: ColimaUI drives Trivy rather than bundling it — its vulnerability database alone is about 1.2 GB and changes daily.
security.no_images_text: Pull or build an image, then come back.
security.pick_image: Pick an image on the left, then scan it.
security.not_scanned: Not scanned yet. Scanning reads the image locally; nothing about it is sent anywhere.
security.scanning: Scanning… the first scan in a while downloads a ~1.2 GB database before it starts.
security.scan_failed: This image could not be scanned
security.total_caption: For sorting a list. The four numbers below are the answer.
security.skipped_rules: {count} rule(s) in this pack could not be run by this build, so their points are out of the total rather than counted as passed.
security.rules_all_pass: Every configuration rule at this level passes.
security.rules_skipped: {count} rule(s) in the pack are newer than this build and were not run.
security.no_findings: No known vulnerabilities in this image, for the database date shown above.
security.alternatives_none: Nothing in the catalog about {image}. That is not a verdict on it — the catalog only covers widely used base images.

triage.clean: Every rule passes at this strictness. Nothing to rank.
triage.headline: Score
triage.headline_note: if every fix below is done
triage.no_ai: Configure an AI provider in Settings first.

autofix.none: Nothing in this Dockerfile can be repaired mechanically. The ranked list above explains what to change by hand.
autofix.applied: Dockerfile patched. You can undo it.
autofix.review_only: Copy this into your Dockerfile once the note above is settled.

security.triage_desc: See what each fix is worth to this image's score, and get the Dockerfile edit for the ones that have one.

history.empty: No history yet. Each scan of this image adds a point.
history.break: Ruler changed — scores before and after are not comparable.
history.title: Score over time

policy.empty: No policy yet. A policy warns you when an image falls below a bar you set — it never stops a container.
policy.needs_a_bar: Set a minimum score or a maximum severity — a rule with neither checks nothing.
policy.warn_only: Policies warn. They never stop or block a container.

watch.label: Rescan running images on a schedule
watch.not_running: Switched on, but not running — scheduled rescans need an active subscription. The switch above still turns them off.
watch.cost: Off by default: a rescan runs a scanner over every running image and may download a vulnerability database.

security.history_desc: Keep every scan, see whether this image is improving, and get warned when it slips below a bar you set.
security.detonation_heading: Run an image and watch it
security.detonation_lead: Scanning says what is inside an image. This says what it does when it runs — in a separate instance that is destroyed afterwards.
security.falco_lead: Runtime events detected by Falco, matched to the compose services you know them by. Falco does the detecting; ColimaUI reads what it reports.

self_heal.title: Self-healing
self_heal.description: Rules that repair a container for you. Every rule only suggests until you say otherwise.
self_heal.feature_desc: Let a rule restart what broke, instead of finding it stopped in the morning.
self_heal.master_hint: Off stops every rule immediately, including anything waiting to run. Rules keep their settings.
self_heal.rule_unhealthy: Restart a container that stays unhealthy
self_heal.rule_crash_loop: Stop a container that is crash-looping
self_heal.rule_disk_full: Suggest a prune when the VM disk fills
self_heal.rule_oom_killed: Suggest a higher memory limit after an OOM kill
self_heal.rule_vm_unresponsive: Restart Colima when it stops answering
self_heal.consequence_restart: This rule will restart the container by itself, without asking you first.
self_heal.consequence_stop: This rule will stop the container by itself. It will stay stopped until you start it.
self_heal.consequence_vm: This rule will restart Colima by itself. Every container on this machine stops while it does.
self_heal.confirm_quota: It will do this at most {count} times an hour.
self_heal.log_empty: Nothing yet. Entries appear here whenever a rule fires, including when one is held back.

detonation.limits_title: This observes behaviour in an isolated environment
detonation.limits_body: The image runs in a separate, disposable Colima instance with no network access and no access to your files. That is a real boundary, but it is not malware-analysis isolation — virtual machine escapes exist. Do not run samples here that you could not afford to have escape.
detonation.desc: Run an image in a disposable isolated instance and see the processes it spawns, the files it changes, and what it writes.

falco.desc: See what Falco detects on your containers, named by compose service rather than container id, with high-priority events raised as alerts.
falco.missing_body: ColimaUI shows runtime events; Falco produces them. It runs inside the Linux VM, not on macOS. The knowledge base has an install guide for Colima.
falco.not_falco_body: A program named falco was found, but it is not the CNCF runtime security tool — most likely the Fastly VCL linter of the same name. Installing via Homebrew gets the wrong one.
falco.installed_title: Falco is installed but not running
falco.installed_body: Start its service inside the VM to begin producing events.
falco.norules_title: Falco is running with no rules loaded
falco.norules_body: It is running and looks healthy, but it has no rules, so it is detecting nothing. An empty list below does not mean nothing happened.
falco.output_title: Falco is running, but not writing events to a file
falco.output_body: Falco is watching your system — ColimaUI just cannot read its output. Enable JSON file output in falco.yaml to see events here.
falco.ready_body: Coverage is whatever your Falco rules cover — {count} loaded.
falco.all_filtered: Every recorded event is hidden by the filters.
falco.no_ai: Configure an AI provider in Settings first.
falco.ai_disclaimer: Written by a model from the events above. It describes and asks; it does not decide whether this is safe.
falco.nothing_to_explain: These events are no longer in the recent window.
